# [America, Unfinished](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=204481531&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA0NDgxNTMxLCJpYXQiOjE3ODMwOTQ4OTAsImV4cCI6MTc4NTY4Njg5MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pmcPtZmYBZ5gom7iC2hv_KC3-BeLmKb5fvU2j-Qh2Pg)
### A Fourth of July reflection on the country we love and the work ahead
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 3
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..e8sS7LNjaVJBuVk47WUhbj3iawH7DAR0Jrz4JBLkrz4?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/america-unfinished?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Friends,
Tomorrow is the Fourth of July, and I hope you get a chance to relax and spend some time with the people you love.
It has been a chaotic, stressful, and heavy time in this country. So I hope you are somewhere where you can breathe and enjoy yourself for a few moments.
If you're in Michigan (the best place in the world to spend the Fourth), maybe you're enjoying a coney dog and a pop and watching the Tigers game. Or maybe you're hiking the U.P., or floating down the Huron with a cooler tied to a tube. Maybe you're headed to the Cherry Festival in Traverse City, or you're planning to watch fireworks light up the lake tomorrow night.
Whatever your day looks like, my wish for you is that you are really there for it, friend. Because those are the sort of Michigan moments I hold close - they're the moments that remind me why I'm in this race, and why I love this state and this country so much.
And I do love it. More than I know how to say.
Tomorrow, America turns 250 years old.
There's a version of patriotism that says America has always been perfect, the work is finished, and we should stop asking hard questions. I don't believe in that version.
I believe in the America that keeps trying to live up to its own promise. The promise that every one of us is equal. That every one of us deserves a real shot. That the people in charge answer to you, the voters, not the other way around.
That promise has been true for some Americans a lot longer than it has been for others. And every bit of progress we have made has been won because somebody somewhere refused to accept things as they were.
Nobody handed us the vote. Nobody handed working people the 40-hour work week. Nobody handed us Social Security, civil rights, or the protections that let working families build a decent life.
People organized. They marched. They voted. They fought. They kept showing up. They had grit. Doggedness. They were relentless.
That is the part of America I believe in most. And that's what I see in the eyes of my fellow Americans when I travel through this great state. I see fight. There is so much good work ahead, and our country needs people who are ready.
We have to fight for the family sitting at the kitchen table, working longer hours than their parents did and still wondering why they are falling further behind.
We have to fight for the woman who cannot get the health care she needs.
We have to fight for the student graduating into an economy that ought to offer a real path to a good job and a decent life, not a lifetime of debt and uncertainty.
I know that sounds like a lot, and it is. **But America 's 250th is a celebration, and to me, it's a reminder that the work is not finished.**
Here is the thing I know about Michigan: We're people who know how to fix things.
When the auto industry was on its knees, Michigan didn't fold. We fought to bring it back. I was proud to serve on President Obama's auto rescue and help save 200,000 Michigan jobs. That is not just some stat to me - it means Michigan families got to stay in their homes, workers got to keep doing what they do best, and communities had a reason to believe in their future.
That is what Michigan does when things get hard. We get stubborn. We get to work.
And that is exactly what we have to do now. That's why I'm working so hard to keep Michigan blue and flip the Senate. Because I believe in America, and especially in Michigan.
This election will still come down to the people of Michigan - what we believe in, what we are willing to fight for, and whether we are going to let Trump and his MAGA allies define the American story or if we're going to put a real check on their chaos agenda.
Keeping Michigan blue means protecting reproductive freedom. It means making gas, groceries, child care, and doctor's visits affordable. It means having a senator who fights for working people instead of doing favors for MAGA billionaires.
That is the work in front of us.
So tomorrow, somewhere between the parade and the fireworks, I will be thinking about how lucky I am to be in this fight with all of you. I will be thinking about the people who came before us and made progress possible. And I will be thinking about the responsibility we have to leave this country fairer, freer, and stronger for whoever comes next.
That's our work. Good thing Michigan has never been afraid of hard work. Let's keep going.
Happy Fourth of July, friends.
More soon.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

| | Every year on the Fourth of July, Americans gather with family and friends to celebrate our nation's independence. This year feels especially significant as our country marks 250 years since its founding.**Like many of you, I have been reflecting on what America truly means to me. When it comes down to it, real patriotism is found in the people.** It lives in the military families who sacrifice so much in service to our country, the teachers who invest in the next generation, and the small business owners who take a chance on a dream. It is driven by parents working long hours just to provide a better future for their children. **Here in El Paso, our community tells a uniquely American story.** We are a border town, a military community, and a home to immigrants, entrepreneurs, and working families. We come from different backgrounds, speak different languages, and worship in different ways, yet we are bound together by a simple, shared belief: every person deserves dignity, opportunity, and a fair chance to succeed. **That, to me, is patriotism. Not just celebrating the ideals our nation was founded upon, but working every day to bring those ideals closer to reality.** That means ensuring every child can receive a quality education. It means access to healthcare for everyone, so families can focus on getting well without worrying about the bill. It means defending the freedom to vote, to speak freely, and to participate fully in our democracy, while creating an economy where hard work is rewarded, and everyone has the opportunity to build a fulfilling life. **America's story has never been one of perfection. It has always been a story of progress.** Generation after generation, ordinary people have pushed our nation to become more inclusive, more just, and more reflective of its highest ideals. This Independence Day, let us celebrate how far we have come while embracing the responsibility we share to keep building a country that lives up to its promise. Happy Fourth of July. clean_body: Our community reminds me what patriotism, opportunity, and service truly look like. | | | | Every year on the Fourth of July, Americans gather with family and friends to celebrate our nation's independence. This year feels especially significant as our country marks 250 years since its founding.Like many of you, I have been reflecting on what America truly means to me. When it comes down to it, real patriotism is found in the people. It lives in the military families who sacrifice so much in service to our country, the teachers who invest in the next generation, and the small business owners who take a chance on a dream. It is driven by parents working long hours just to provide a better future for their children. Here in El Paso, our community tells a uniquely American story. We are a border town, a military community, and a home to immigrants, entrepreneurs, and working families. We come from different backgrounds, speak different languages, and worship in different ways, yet we are bound together by a simple, shared belief: every person deserves dignity, opportunity, and a fair chance to succeed. That, to me, is patriotism. Not just celebrating the ideals our nation was founded upon, but working every day to bring those ideals closer to reality. That means ensuring every child can receive a quality education. It means access to healthcare for everyone, so families can focus on getting well without worrying about the bill. It means defending the freedom to vote, to speak freely, and to participate fully in our democracy, while creating an economy where hard work is rewarded, and everyone has the opportunity to build a fulfilling life. America's story has never been one of perfection. It has always been a story of progress. Generation after generation, ordinary people have pushed our nation to become more inclusive, more just, and more reflective of its highest ideals. This Independence Day, let us celebrate how far we have come while embracing the responsibility we share to keep building a country that lives up to its promise. Happy Fourth of July. Here's the deal, team: Voter registration work happens all year long, not just in the summer and through the lead-in to the deadlines ahead of Election Day.
There's no better way to defend our fundamental right to vote than by registering a ton of new voters and winning critical local, state, and federal elections. Our access to the ballot -- from vote-by-mail to drop boxes to early voting and more -- depends on being able to pass laws that are pro-voter, not pro-incumbent politician.
As little as $3 supports our work to register a new voter. Please, RUSH $30 or more right now to help us register 10 new voters to fight back at the polls >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=070326_1&amount=30]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
MS NOW: ‘The largest investment ever’: DNC launches voter registration drive [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=070326_1&amount=30]
The 2025 elections showed us a valuable truth, folks: Voter participation is increasing in all the right ways.
Voter registration activity increased across the country. According to the team at National Voter Registration Day, New York recorded more registrations for their 2025 events than in 2024, and California saw similar increases. Earlier this fall it looked like voter participation was going to make a real jump, even in a so-called "off-year".
Then Election Day came. New Jersey had more voters turn out for a gubernatorial election than they had in 20 years. Crucial counties in Pennsylvania saw their highest turnout levels in almost 15 years. New York City reached a turnout percentage unseen in over five decades.
We can drive even higher levels of participation when voters understand the stakes and feel like their vote matters , just like it did last November. That's why our voter registration efforts are so important, and why we work on it all year long.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=070326_1&amount=30]

Pundits in Virginia said they could have called the election results when they saw the first turnout numbers from the major college campus locations around the state. That's the kind of impact these young voters can have.
Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
The upcoming midterm election will determine whether our democracy stays mired in the darkness and conspiracy theories we hear every day or if we can reclaim our rights -- from voting to choice and more -- and march forward to a better future.

name: Chloe Cole
subject: "Would you rather have a dead daughter or a living son?"
body:
I was 12 years old. I was not suicidal. They lied to my parents — and nobody stopped them.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e7097594/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvcjZRc1Z1WFRLSw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MDM/LbmNsejFCdGxvRQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNSdlBTR2VOSE1EbHhscw/gakfhmg/s4ncd2c9995)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | Friend, **"Would you rather have a dead daughter or a living son?"** That is what a doctor said to my parents. I was 12 years old. I was in the next room. **I was not suicidal.** I was a confused girl who had started puberty early and felt different from everyone around her. I had older brothers. I didn't fit in with the girls in my class. I didn't know why. I just knew something hurt. But that doctor didn't ask about any of that. She looked at my frightened parents — two people who loved me more than anything in the world — and handed them a choice no parent should ever have to make. _"A dead daughter. Or a living son."_ My parents chose me. They didn't know the choice wasn't real. **They didn't know they were being lied to.** They didn't know that what happened next would take something from me that no surgery, no hormone, no court verdict can ever give back.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**At 13, I had my first testosterone injection.** As a result, I will likely have medical complications for the rest of my life. My fertility is still unknown. **At 15, a surgeon at a Kaiser facility removed my breasts.** I was a child. I didn't fully understand what breastfeeding was. I didn't understand what losing that meant for my future. **No one at that facility stopped and asked whether I might change my mind.** A few months after surgery, I started to question everything. A year later, I knew the truth. I was a girl. I had always been a girl. I was a girl who hated puberty and had no one to tell her that was normal. **At 16 — after the surgery — I became suicidal.** This was the exact nightmare the doctors told my parents they were preventing.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
The doctors who performed those procedures have not once reached out to help me. They called it care. There was no jury. No verdict. No accountability. **Until now.** You knew something was wrong. Maybe you couldn't name it. But when you saw what was being done to children like me, something in you refused to accept it as medicine. **You were right. I am proof of that.** **The Center for American Liberty took my case.** Kaiser tried to bury it in secret arbitration. A California appeals court said no. My case goes to open court. On January 30, 2026, the first detransitioner malpractice lawsuit in American history reached a jury. Six ordinary Americans heard the facts. **They sided with a young woman just like me.** My trial is next. **April 5, 2027. Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. A California courtroom.** The doctors who signed off on what was done to me will sit in front of a jury for the first time. **Friend, that jury will be made up of people exactly like you.** People who trusted their instincts. People who looked at what was done to a child and applied common sense and the law.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every dollar gets us one step closer to that courtroom. I am not the only one. There are hundreds of us — young men and women who heard the same things I heard, who trusted the same doctors, who are living with the same consequences. Most of them have never seen the inside of a courtroom. Because the hospitals have a playbook: delay, arbitrate, settle, seal. No jury. No verdict. No accountability. Kaiser quietly stopped performing gender surgeries on patients under 19 in August 2025. They didn't announce a change of heart. They cited "significant risks being created for health systems." Meaning: lawsuits. **Meaning: people like you** , who refused to stay quiet. **That playbook only works if you walk away.** You haven't walked away yet.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Friend, I don't know you personally. But I know something about you. I know that when everyone around you said this was none of your business — that children's medical decisions weren't yours to question — something in you refused to accept that. That refusal matters. It matters to me. It matters to every detransitioner who has never seen the inside of a courtroom. It matters to the next confused 12-year-old girl sitting in a waiting room while a doctor tells her parents there is only one way to save her. **You are the reason that story doesn't have to end the way mine did.** You can be the reason I walk into that courtroom on April 5 with the strongest legal team in the country. You can be the reason the doctors who signed off on what was done to me finally face a jury. **You can be the reason the next girl** has someone standing in the way.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
You knew something was wrong. April 5, 2027 is what happens when people like you decide to do something about it. **Thank you for being one of those people.**
---
Chloe Cole On behalf of the Center for American Liberty
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**P.S.** April 5, 2027. That's my trial date against Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. They tried arbitration, delays, sealed records — every tool in the playbook to keep what they did out of a courtroom. The courts said no. The first detransitioner lawsuit already went to a jury. They sided with a young woman just like me. Now I need to walk in on April 5 with the strongest team possible. Your $100 today goes straight to funding this fight. You've known this was wrong. This is your chance to do something about it.
---

As a result, I will likely have medical complications for the rest of my life. My fertility is still unknown. At 15, a surgeon at a Kaiser facility removed my breasts. I was a child. I didn't fully understand what breastfeeding was. I didn't understand what losing that meant for my future. No one at that facility stopped and asked whether I might change my mind. A few months after surgery, I started to question everything. A year later, I knew the truth. I was a girl. I had always been a girl. I was a girl who hated puberty and had no one to tell her that was normal. At 16 — after the surgery — I became suicidal. This was the exact nightmare the doctors told my parents they were preventing. The doctors who performed those procedures have not once reached out to help me. They called it care. There was no jury. No verdict. No accountability. Until now. You knew something was wrong. Maybe you couldn't name it. But when you saw what was being done to children like me, something in you refused to accept it as medicine. You were right. I am proof of that. The Center for American Liberty took my case. Kaiser tried to bury it in secret arbitration. A California appeals court said no. My case goes to open court. On January 30, 2026, the first detransitioner malpractice lawsuit in American history reached a jury. Six ordinary Americans heard the facts. They sided with a young woman just like me. My trial is next. April 5, 2027. Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. A California courtroom. The doctors who signed off on what was done to me will sit in front of a jury for the first time. Friend, that jury will be made up of people exactly like you. People who trusted their instincts. People who looked at what was done to a child and applied common sense and the law. Every dollar gets us one step closer to that courtroom. I am not the only one. There are hundreds of us — young men and women who heard the same things I heard, who trusted the same doctors, who are living with the same consequences. Most of them have never seen the inside of a courtroom. Because the hospitals have a playbook: delay, arbitrate, settle, seal. No jury. No verdict. No accountability. Kaiser quietly stopped performing gender surgeries on patients under 19 in August 2025. They didn't announce a change of heart. They cited "significant risks being created for health systems." Meaning: lawsuits. Meaning: people like you , who refused to stay quiet. That playbook only works if you walk away. You haven't walked away yet. Friend, I don't know you personally. But I know something about you. I know that when everyone around you said this was none of your business — that children's medical decisions weren't yours to question — something in you refused to accept that. That refusal matters. It matters to me. It matters to every detransitioner who has never seen the inside of a courtroom. It matters to the next confused 12-year-old girl sitting in a waiting room while a doctor tells her parents there is only one way to save her. You are the reason that story doesn't have to end the way mine did. You can be the reason I walk into that courtroom on April 5 with the strongest legal team in the country. You can be the reason the doctors who signed off on what was done to me finally face a jury. You can be the reason the next girl has someone standing in the way. You knew something was wrong. April 5, 2027 is what happens when people like you decide to do something about it. Thank you for being one of those people. Chloe Cole On behalf of the Center for American Liberty P.S. April 5, 2027. That's my trial date against Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. They tried arbitration, delays, sealed records — every tool in the playbook to keep what they did out of a courtroom. The courts said no. The first detransitioner lawsuit already went to a jury. They sided with a young woman just like me. Now I need to walk in on April 5 with the strongest team possible. Your $100 today goes straight to funding this fight. You've known this was wrong. This is your chance to do something about it. | | | The Center for American Liberty is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit charitable organization fighting against growing anti-free speech and anti-civil liberties trends. # [Scorching heat shatters records as America's biggest grid hits breaking point](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A dangerous heat wave sweeping the central and eastern U.S. is pushing electricity demand to near-record levels ahead of the July 4 weekend, **[forcing America's largest grid operator to secure emergency powers](https://substack.com/redirect/c3712e9d-66ff-463f-a7e0-c460fbd45cb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while triggering travel delays and price surges.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Record Demand Forecast Issued:** PJM Interconnection expects electricity use to hit one hundred sixty six thousand one hundred forty seven megawatts on Thursday surpassing the two thousand six summer peak of one hundred sixty five thousand five hundred sixty three megawatts.
* **Emergency Authority Granted:** The grid operator received federal approval under Section two hundred two c to curtail data centers and large users with backup generators plus temporary environmental relief for power plants through July third.
* **Travel Disruptions Warned:** **[Amtrak plans reduced speeds and delays between eleven a.m. and seven p.m. through July 4th](https://substack.com/redirect/fb3f2c78-e394-4bcd-8dda-5a4e7cfae460?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while New Jersey Transit Delta and Illinois roads also face heat related impacts on equipment and pavement.
* **Conservation Calls Issued:** New York City Mayor urged residents to set air conditioning to seventy eight degrees turn off unused electronics run appliances off peak and stay inside amid soaring wholesale power prices up over two hundred percent in parts of the region.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Program Partnership Joined:** The bank joins other major financial firms including Citi JPMorgan Chase Bank of America and Vanguard in backing the initiative.
* **Account Launch Details:** Trump Accounts roll out July 4th with low cost index fund investments allowing parents up to five thousand dollars annual contributions and employers up to two thousand five hundred dollars.

# [Oil dethroned? Natural gas surges toward number one US energy source](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Natural gas is **[projected to overtake petroleum as the leading U.S. energy source](https://substack.com/redirect/a34aa545-69dc-4c0c-bc84-1e65ecc5a148?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by 2030 after closing the gap in 2025 driven by shale production electrification and rising demand from data centers and electric vehicles.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Energy Consumption Shifted:** In 2025 natural gas made up 36% of U.S. consumption nearly matching petroleum at 76% ending oil's seventy five year dominance.
* **Demand Drivers Identified:** Electrification EVs and data centers boost gas fired power plants which now generate more than 40% of U.S. grid electricity according to agency data.
* **Production Revolution Cited:** Shale revolution and horizontal drilling unlocked reserves displacing coal with over one hundred coal plants replaced or converted since 2011.
* **Future Growth Forecast:** Energy Information Administration expects gas demand to rise 3.4% between 2025 and 2027 outpacing petroleum's 0.6% increase.

Henrico County in Virginia is asking employees to conserve electricity as rates climb 25% adding an estimated $5 million dollars in costs next year citing data center growth as a key factor driving demand.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Historical Comparison Made:** The manager compared the austerity steps to cost saving efforts during the Great Recession more than 15 years ago while seeking 3% budget reductions.
* **Data Center Role Noted:** Virginia leads the nation with the most data centers concentrated in northern and central regions substantially increasing overall state energy demand and system costs.

# [Zuckerberg confesses ai agents developing far slower than planned](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees at an internal town hall that AI agent development has not accelerated as anticipated during a major restructuring that included 10% layoffs and reassignments to AI teams.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b289146f-f46f-433e-89bb-4e2344541e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Restructuring Shortcomings Acknowledged:** The reorganization with roughly 7,000 employees shifted to AI was not as clean as planned and timing of changes was miscalculated according to the executive.
* **Development Trajectory Noted:** The trajectory of agentic development over the last four months has not accelerated in the way expected despite earlier optimism around tools like Claude Code.
* **Investment Scale Detailed:** Meta is projected to spend up to $145 billion dollars on AI infrastructure this year part of broader Big Tech outlays exceeding $700 billion dollars.
* **Benefits Timeline Updated:** The company expects more significant gains from AI investments to appear within the next three to six months following the changes aimed at efficiency and infrastructure funding.

Peter,
This weekend, millions of Americans will gather with family and friends, march in parades, fire up the grill, and watch fireworks as we celebrate America's 250th birthday.
When I think about what makes America extraordinary, I think about our people.
It’s the farmworkers who feed our families. The public school teachers who prepare the next generation. The nurses who care for our loved ones. The first responders who answer the call when we need them. The workers, entrepreneurs, and small business owners who keep our communities strong.
That’s why I’m most proud to be on Team America.
To me, Team America means investing in our people—not endless wars. It means making college and trade school free, capping child care costs at $10 a day, rebuilding American manufacturing, rewarding work instead of wealth, and putting working families ahead of billionaire donors and special interests.
That’s the America I’m fighting for.
Two hundred and fifty years ago, our founders launched an extraordinary experiment in self-government. Every generation since has had the responsibility to move our country closer to its promise. Now it's our turn.
As you celebrate this Fourth of July, I'd love to hear from you.
What gives you hope about America's future?
Send me a text at (650) 999-9610 and let me know how you're celebrating—and what you hope the next 250 years will bring.
Thank you for your activism and all that you do.
Happy Fourth of July!
– Ro
Wait! One more thing–
Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. name: Abigail Lowell
subject: Can I share a fun redwoods fact?
body:
Dear Peter,

I’ll admit that I’m a bit of a nerd when it comes to the redwoods.

My love for these forests is what drew me to Save the Redwoods League. I went from a Redwoods Rising Fellow to a full-time staff member supporting this critical restoration work.

And, since we just launched a special Redwoods Rising quiz , [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising-quiz?sourceid=1170305&ms=RR_EM10&utm_campaign=K2D-1170305&utm_source=ea-engagement&utm_medium=email] I thought this was a perfect time to share some of my favorite fun facts about the redwoods!

* Redwoods and salmon are more connected than you think—redwoods provide cool, clear waters for spawning grounds, while salmon provide the trees with key nutrients after they spawn and die.

* Coast redwoods get up to 30% of their annual water intake from fog! With redwood regions becoming warmer and drier amidst climate change, the need for science-driven restoration work is more important than ever.

* It’s a misconception that fires are always bad for forests. Prescribed burns and natural low-intensity fires can help clear out crowded underbrush , recycle nutrients into the soil, and stimulate plant and tree growth.

* Redwoods often have cavities or tunnels in their trunks! These are called basal hollows, and form when hot fires get through to the interior heartwood of the tree.

I could go on... but I’ll stop there and give you a chance to take our Redwoods Rising quiz and test your knowledge! [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising-quiz?sourceid=1170305&ms=RR_EM10&utm_campaign=K2D-1170305&utm_source=ea-engagement&utm_medium=email]

I went from a Redwoods Rising Fellow to a full-time staff member supporting this critical restoration work. And, since we just launched a special Redwoods Rising quiz , [] I thought this was a perfect time to share some of my favorite fun facts about the redwoods! Redwoods and salmon are more connected than you think—redwoods provide cool, clear waters for spawning grounds, while salmon provide the trees with key nutrients after they spawn and die. Coast redwoods get up to 30% of their annual water intake from fog! With redwood regions becoming warmer and drier amidst climate change, the need for science-driven restoration work is more important than ever. It’s a misconception that fires are always bad for forests. Prescribed burns and natural low-intensity fires can help clear out crowded underbrush , recycle nutrients into the soil, and stimulate plant and tree growth. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Friend, Tomorrow, America will celebrate its 250th birthday, but most rights that we hold dear are under attack. Trump wants to take away our right to vote. He’s trying to ban the U.S. Postal Service from delivering mail-in ballots, even as 63% of voters in my district vote by mail. He is violating our due process rights, caging immigrants while using the Dept. of Justice to attack his perceived political foes. He’s also attacking our free speech rights, encouraging decades-long sentences for lawful and peaceful protest. He has illegally taken us to war and committed war crimes. He and his family have personally profited from his presidency to the tune of billions of dollars. He has weakened workers’ rights, environmental standards, and the government agencies meant to protect our communities and our health. Through our Rooted in Community Leadership PAC, we are fighting back on two fronts:
* Electing pro-democracy, democratic socialist, and anti-war leaders to Congress and to positions up and down the ballot.
* Training the leaders of tomorrow, today.

This is how I need your help today: Right now, we’re training 15 Democracy Summer Fellows on how to take back and strengthen our democracy. They’re learning everything from door-knocking to phone-banking to voter protection. And they’re taking weekly history classes; next week’s session is **_“The Supreme Court, Political Corruption, and the Authoritarian Attack on Government.”_** Here is one of our Fellows — Adam — door-knocking for U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Dear Peter,
For the first time ever, the Republican Party will hold a Midterm Convention -- a historic, one-of-a-kind event. President Donald J. Trump, Vice President J.D. Vance, the Republican National Committee and Republicans from around the country will come together in Dallas for a national celebration heading into the 2026 midterms -- a moment to unite our Party, energize our grassroots, and showcase our candidates on the national stage, all while celebrating our nation, our achievements, and our bright future.
"We are going to celebrate the GREAT AMERICAN COMEBACK, and the incredible successes of the American People who transformed our Country through the America First Agenda. . . . It will be a RALLY like none other!" - President Donald J. Trump
If you're even considering going, apply to join the Massachuestts delegation right away. More information below.
To Victory in November!
---
|
---
Amy Carnevale Chair, Massachusetts Republican Party
---
The Great American Comeback Midterm Convention September 9-10, 2026 | American Airlines Center | Dallas, Texas

## What We're Celebrating
* The America First Agenda: No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security, stronger borders, the safest communities in our history, lower costs, and real affordability for American families.
* More jobs, American energy dominance, and the hardworking Americans, innovators, entrepreneurs, manufacturers, first responders, and job creators powering our nation's Golden Age.
* America's 250th Birthday -- together, we are building the foundation for the next 250 years of American Greatness.

## What This Event Is
* A special ceremonial national gathering -- not a nominating convention.
* A celebration of our Party's vision and candidates, built to mobilize voters ahead of November.

## Key Distinctions from Conventions
* No nominating delegates. There is no credentialing process, as this is not a delegate or alternate event associated with a nomination.
* Tickets, not credentials. Each state party will receive and distribute a set allocation of tickets. The MassGOP will accept applications for tickets and applicants are subject to vetting at both the state and national level.

## Logistics at a Glance
* Dates: Wednesday, September 9 - Thursday, September 10, 2026
* Venue: American Airlines Center, 2500 Victory Ave, Dallas, TX 75219
* Ticket allocations: The allocation process will move quickly. There is a $20 processing fee per application.
* Dues: If selected, you must pay your dues within 48 hours, which are expected to increase from the 2024 Convention Dues of $500.
* Hotels: The MassGOP will reserve an allocation of hotel rooms for ticket holders once the official hotels are released by the RNC.
* Transportation: Transportation to and from Dallas will be on your own. Transportation to and from the RNC hotels to the American Airlines Center will be provided to all official ticket holders.
* Overall Costs: Upwards of $3,000
* Questions: Contact the MassGOP at [info@massgop.com](mailto:info@massgop.com)

**Peter, the Transgender community is under attack in America.**

body:
I couldn’t be more different from Mark Baisley.
---
**Lauren Boebert’s hand-picked candidate is chomping at the bit to flip this seat. He can’t wait to rubber-stamp the president’s cruel agenda.** _Can you believe that, Derek!?_ State Senator Mark Baisley has pledged to partner with the Trump administration. He’s vowed to limit abortion access and supports overturning common-sense gun control. [**We can’t let someone like this EVER represent Colorado in the U.S. Senate. Will you rush a split donation between my campaign and the DNC to help us stop a red wave from coming to Colorado and take back the Senate? And at number one, well, you're just going to have to watch to see what number one is!

I'll be straight with you.

I do not like sending emails like this. Never have. But I owe you the truth about where my campaign stands.

We set a goal for this month. A real number we have to hit to fund the campaign and win this race.

_**Right now, we are short.**_

**The Radical Left is throwing tens of millions of dollars at this seat.** Dark money. Out-of-state cash. Coastal donors who have never set foot in Arkansas but want to dictate who represents us in Washington.

_That is why I am writing to you today._

I need patriots stepping up — every week, every day, every hour of this month — to keep this campaign on offense. Every day we wait is a day they get bolder. Every dollar that comes in is one more piece of armor for the fight ahead.

I have kept the promise to fight back against the Liberal Mob. I am not stopping now. Not while our border is under siege. Not while Communist China is on the march. Not while the Radical Left works to undo everything Arkansas stands for.

name: Wes Moore
subject: One promise above everything else
body:
This is what I said.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1585%2E1086043%2E9fbLQz)
When I ran for governor, I made one promise above everything else, Peter:
**That we would build a Maryland that leaves no one behind.**
That meant the kid in Baltimore who needed better schools. The family in Prince George's who needed to feel safe. The worker who needed a real shot at a livable wage.
We've delivered — not perfectly, but relentlessly.
➡️ We reduced homicides in Maryland – to the lowest level in decades.
➡️ We raised teacher salaries and brought new businesses back at a rate we haven't seen since before the pandemic.
➡️ We lowered energy bills for families across the state by $200 million.
And make no mistake: We’re just getting started. **_But to continue this work, I need your help._**
Dan Cox and his MAGA allies will stop at nothing to make me a one-term governor. They're ready to tear back all of the progress that we've made together. **I need your help to make sure that they don't succeed.**

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: Two Parades. One Proud American.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
Have a Happy Fourth Johnson County!

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| |

Friends,This Fourth of July means a little more to me.As a proud member of the Daughters of the American Revolution, I'm reminded that our freedom wasn't guaranteed. It was earned through extraordinary courage, sacrifice, and an unwavering belief that self-government was worth fighting for.Now 250 years later, we're the beneficiaries of that legacy. Our responsibility is to protect it, strengthen it, and leave it better for the next generation.That's why I love serving this community, why I’m running for Johnson County Commission Chair and _**why I'm not taking the holiday off.**_ I'll be celebrating the best way I know how: meeting neighbors, shaking hands, and walking in not one, but **two** Fourth of July parades!**Lenexa Fourth of July Parade - rolls at 10:00 am
Stilwell Fourth of July Parade - rolls at 6:00 pm**If you're attending either parade, please say hi! You can’t miss our entry - I’ll be the one walking behind our campaign trailer, smiling, handing out candy and dog treats. From my family to yours, I wish you a safe, joyful, and meaningful Independence Day.God bless you, God bless Johnson County, and God bless the United States of America.**Karen Crnkovich****Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair**

| | Dear Friend,

As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, we reflect not only on our independence, but also on the enduring ideals that have guided our nation for two and a half centuries — life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

America 250 is a moment to honor the generations who built, defended, and strengthened this country, while recommitting ourselves to the work of preserving freedom and opportunity for future generations.

As we gather with family, friends, and neighbors, may we celebrate the spirit of unity, service, and resilience that defines our nation, and take time to appreciate those who have sacrificed for her.

From my family to yours, I wish you a safe and joyful celebration. God bless America!
---
| Sincerely,

Congressman Vince Fong

body:
Lizzie Happy Independence Day Graphic [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Lizzie%20Happy%20Independence%20Day%20Graphic.jpg]

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, I’ve been reading, watching, listening, and thinking a lot about what that anniversary means. The Declaration we celebrate was revolutionary in every sense of the word. The history of the United States is very much one of expanding the Declaration’s promise to all of its citizens, slowly and imperfectly. We have not always lived up to our ideals of equality and justice for all, but we have not abandoned them.
Generations of Americans have fought to expand the rights first articulated in the Declaration to all Americans, and that work continues to this day. The progress of the past feels in peril in the present. From the White House to state houses across the country, we are seeing attacks on our rights and freedoms, on the progress so many have worked so hard and so long to make.
And that is why my celebration of Independence Day and its 250th anniversary starts with thanks to the people who, over the last 250 years, have worked for liberty, equality, and justice for all. And that includes all of the people who have volunteered their time, talents, and treasure to help our campaign and our effort to do our part in protecting and advancing American democracy and the ideals we celebrate today. Our challenges aren't going away— but neither are we .
As I think about those challenges, I keep thinking of the words of President Clinton who said in his first inaugural address, “There is nothing that is wrong with America that can’t be fixed by what is right with America.”
Together, we can do anything.

name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
subject: The America that welcomed my family is disappearing
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
This weekend, America turns 250 years old.
I've been thinking about what that means. I've been thinking about what this country actually meant to one family — my family — and what it means that the things that made our story possible are being systematically torn apart.
My parents came to this country with virtually nothing. They came because they believed that America would be there for them. That if they worked hard enough, sacrificed enough, held on long enough, this country would meet them halfway.
And it did.
We moved into public housing and relied on food stamps when times got tough. I went to public schools in Peoria, Illinois — District 150 — where teachers showed up every day for kids like me, kids who looked different and spoke differently and came from families that didn't have a safety net beyond what this country provided.
With the help of those schools and programs, plus loans, scholarships, and the money I saved working at McDonald's, I went to college and law school. Then Congress.That is the American Dream. It’s more than a campaign slogan or simple talking point. It’s a real thing that happened to a real family because this country had built something — a floor beneath working people, a ladder out of poverty, a set of institutions that said: we see you, and we will not let you fall through.I am standing here today because of that floor. Because of that ladder. Because of those institutions.
And Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are dismantling them piece by piece.
The Department of Education — gutted. The same public schools that gave me a fighting chance are being starved of resources while billionaires get tax cuts and vouchers to send their kids to private academies. I went to those public schools. I know what they meant. And I know what it means to take that away from the next kid who needs them.
SNAP — cut. The food stamps that kept my family fed are being ripped away from millions of Americans who are doing exactly what my parents did: working hard, holding on, and trusting that this country wouldn't let their children go hungry. That trust is being betrayed.
Public housing — on the chopping block. The roof over our heads when we had nothing else. Gone, for families who have nothing else today.
And the immigration system — the pathway that brought my parents here, that brought millions of families here, that made America the place people dreamed of reaching — is being actively, deliberately, cruelly dismantled. Not reformed. Not improved. Weaponized against the very people who come here with the same faith my parents had fifty years ago.
I want to be clear about what this means.
It means that if my family arrived in America today, our story ends differently. It means the floor isn't there. The ladder isn't there. The kid with the hard-to-pronounce name doesn't get to go to college. Doesn't get to Congress. Doesn't get to fight for the next family that needs it.
The America that saved my family is not the America of today. And on its 250th birthday, I think we owe it the honesty of saying that out loud.
This is why I started Equal Opportunity Now. Not because I want to relitigate the past. But because I refuse to accept that this is inevitable. Because there are leaders out there right now who are ready to fight to restore what's being taken. Because the American Dream is not a relic. It is a living thing that must be defended by every generation that benefited from it.
My father made me promise to make sure this country was there for the next families who needed it.
I intend to keep that promise.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect the leaders who will fight to restore the America that made our stories possible? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TO ELECT LEADERS NATIONWIDE! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Two hundred and fifty years.
It's worth fighting for.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

| | | Fellow American, **I'll get straight to the point because there isn't time to waste.** A brand-new poll from the _New York Times_ and Siena College just dropped -- and it shows me and my far-left Democrat opponent, James Talarico, tied at 47% each in the race for U.S. Senate in Texas. _This is a blaring alarm warning for all conservatives!_ Texas hasn't sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in almost 40 years -- since 1988. And right now, the liberal media and Democrat donors smell blood in the water. They think this is their year to **flip Texas blue** with Talarico... _Here's what the poll found that should alarm every conservative in this state:_ **Talarico is leading me by 27 points among independents, and he is up 18 points with women voters overall ...****** This is a man who stood on the floor of the Texas House and declared "God is nonbinary," and who has argued that there are "six biological sexes." He says the American Flag is a complicated symbol... This is who the media is falsely calling a moderate "rising star," which is allowing Talarico to slip under the radar of many voters. name: Molly Gray
subject: This July 4th weekend
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Hi Peter,
I just finished marching in the Brandon parade, and will be in Montpelier this evening and in Williston tomorrow.
Before I sign off for the weekend, I wanted to wish you and your family a safe, fun, and meaningful Fourth—and share some of what has been on my mind.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/Copy%20of%20Waterbury%20crop.JPG]
Being an American, a citizen, and a patriot – it is complicated these days.
But what gives me hope and what I like to focus on is who we can be on our best days.
I also like to focus on our small and mighty state of Vermont, our strong (and evolving) values and what we can do, in these extremely challenging times.
We can be a place where free speech is still protected and where people don’t live in fear of persecution or deportation for sharing their views.
We can be a welcoming and safe place for immigrants and recognize the talent, hard work, and richness our new neighbors bring to our communities.
We can be a place where the freedom to love and be loved is equal for everyone.
We can be a place where healthcare, affordable housing, a good paying job, and economic security are basic rights, and fundamental for everyone.
My list goes on...
But most of all, we can control how we show up. We can choose kindness over cruelty. We can care for one another, see the best in each other, and realize there is so much more that unites us than divides us. We can make our children proud.
That’s what patriotism means to me, and that’s what I’ll be thinking about and celebrating this weekend.
I wish you a safe, happy, and memorable Fourth of July.
I hope to see you out there!
-Molly Gray

**Happy Independence Day! 🇺🇸✍️🎇**
This Fourth of July is unlike any other. Tomorrow, America celebrates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence—a quarter of a millennium since a small group of courageous men declared that our rights come from God, not government, and that liberty was worth risking everything to defend.
For 250 years, generations of Americans have answered the call to preserve that promise. They've served on battlefields, in their communities, in public office, in classrooms, in churches, and around family tables—passing the ideals of freedom from one generation to the next.
At Rocky Mountain Voice, we're grateful to be part of that continuing story. Our mission has always been to inform, equip, and encourage Coloradans with trustworthy reporting because an informed citizenry is essential to a free republic.
As you celebrate with family and friends today, we hope you'll take a moment to reflect on the extraordinary blessings of living in the United States and remember those who have sacrificed to protect the freedoms we enjoy.
From all of us at Rocky Mountain Voice, thank you for reading, supporting independent journalism, and being part of this community.
_**Happy Independence Day—and here's to America's next 250 years.**_ 🇺🇸
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, July 3, 2026.

[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Nick Shirley spent Saturday night walking the Freedom Fest audience through the questions that have taken him from hotels near Denver International Airport to empty daycare centers in Minnesota and apartment complexes in Aurora.
Interviewed by Jeff Hunt, co-host of the Jeff and Bill Show on Denver’s 710 KNUS, Shirley spent less time talking about what he uncovered than how he uncovered it. Long before a Minnesota daycare investigation made him nationally known, Shirley found himself in Colorado after repeatedly hearing migrants at the southern border mention the same destination. Denver.
He came to look. “You guys are from Latin America? It’s cold in Denver,” he remembered asking. “What are you guys doing in Denver?”

**[Money didn’t win Colorado’s primary. The ground game did.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Republican primary for governor remains too close to call, with Victor Marx leading Barb Kirkmeyer by just 2,181 votes out of more than 500,000 cast — while the Colorado Conservative Leadership Fund, which put over $325,000 into door-knocking operations, won at least five of seven races it contested, proving that boots on the ground outperform big ad buys.
* A Democrat dark-money network funneled $1.5 million through six progressive-sounding front committees — four filing from the same Durango address — backed almost entirely by an anonymous labor-led nonprofit, then spent every dollar on mailers and digital ads with zero canvassing, and lost four of five races it targeted.
* The primary's biggest takeaway for November: more than half of Colorado's active voters are unaffiliated, the Democrat ballot-ratio advantage reflected competitive races drawing strategic voters rather than ideology, and Republicans — who haven't won a statewide race since 2016 — must expand beyond their base to win the middle if they want to change that streak in the fall.

**QUOTE OF THE DAY** ___"The Second Day of July 1776, will be the most memorable Epocha, in the History of America. I am apt to believe that it will be celebrated, by succeeding Generations, as the great anniversary Festival. It ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations from one End of this Continent to the other from this Time forward forever more. You will think me transported with Enthusiasm but I am not. -- I am well aware of the Toil and Blood and Treasure, that it will cost Us to maintain this Declaration, and support and defend these States. -- Yet through all the Gloom I can see the Rays of ravishing Light and Glory. I can see that the End is more than worth all the Means. And that Posterity will tryumph in that Days Transaction, even altho We should rue it, which I trust in God We shall not."_

— John Adams, writing to Abigail, about the Continental Congress' vote in favor of independence on July 2, 1776

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Oversight is not a crime
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
LaMonica McIver is being prosecuted for doing her job.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260703-6430-footer&t=1&akid=6430%2E420207%2EvA4FBk)
Peter,
Let me be clear — oversight is not a crime. **It is a constitutional duty.**
Yet, Rep. LaMonica McIver is facing _17 years in prison_ for doing exactly what she was elected to do by showing up to conduct congressional oversight at an ICE facility in New Jersey.
**LaMonica has consistently stepped up to protect immigrant communities and demand accountability from ICE. Now she is being prosecuted for it.**
Women of color have _always_ stood at the front lines of protecting our communities and our rights, and LaMonica is no different.
**However, she is not alone in this fight.**
I am proud to stand alongside her, and will continue to challenge abuse of power, defend civil liberties, and fight for justice and accountability no matter who is in the White House.
This case is about more than one member of Congress. It is about setting a precedent.
When a sitting lawmaker can be prosecuted for conducting oversight, it sends a message to every public official in this country: _speak up, ask questions, and you could be next._
That is how accountability gets weakened — not all at once, but by making an example out of one person to intimidate the rest.
**And that should concern all of us.**
Because if lawmakers can be punished for oversight, then no one who speaks truth to power is safe.
[**If you believe elected officials should be able to do their jobs without fear of political prosecution, will you split a contribution between LaMonica McIver and me to help us keep up the fight in Congress?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260703.n1YXk-&refcode=em20260703-6430&t=2&akid=6430%2E420207%2EvA4FBk)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

subject: We’re going on offense against the GOP

body:
We have a large slate of red-to-blue races that could break the GOP’s grip on power.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260703-1&t=1&akid=3682%2E587540%2EIPWUqy)
The far right doesn’t belong in the headlines anymore, Peter.
It belongs in the history books, as a cautionary tale of what happens when extremism goes unchecked for too long.
**That’s why Leaders We Deserve is working to flip red seats blue this cycle.**
We have a large slate of red-to-blue seats this cycle that are absolutely flippable with the proper resources behind their campaigns:
🔄 **Randy Villegas** (CA-22) — his race will decide who controls the House in a district Trump won by just about 2%.
🔄 **Tim Hayes** (PA-HD-143) — taking on a GOP incumbent in a seat Democrats nearly flipped in 2024.
🔄 **Kristian Carranza** (TX-HD-118) — back for a rematch after coming within 4% of a win last cycle.
🔄 **Trevor Jung (WI-SD-21)** — challenging a Republican in a seat that's slipping out of his grasp (this state legislative race will likely cost more than most congressional races because it is so critical).
🔄 **Ken McCool** (NC-HD-105) — taking on a sitting GOP incumbent critical to making sure we are able to protect the Democratic governor’s veto power.
🔄 **Jane Aman** (FL-HD-37) — running in one of Florida's most competitive battleground districts that the GOP won by just 485 votes last cycle.
🔄 **Cat Clayton** (MO-HD-105) — fighting to flip a seat Republicans have held for 15 years and is essential to breaking the GOP super majority in the state.
These are races that will break GOP supermajorities, flip state legislatures, and help ensure there’s a real check on Trump’s dangerous agenda.
_This is a must-win election year._ And the truth is, our best shot at flipping these seats isn’t by playing it safe. Protecting the status quo is exactly what fed the disillusionment that has driven an entire generation of young voters to despair.
**Our work is the solution to that disillusionment.** We have to go all in on bold leaders who will actually center working-class priorities and offer a vision for the future that sparks hope, not apathy or fear.
**[If you’re with us, will you pitch in $5 to help Leaders We Deserve flip these critical red seats blue and break the GOP’s grip on power?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260703_1_flip.Rz1c-W&refcode=em20260703-3682&amount=5&t=2&akid=3682%2E587540%2EIPWUqy)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Do you believe in my vision for New Mexico? Add your name!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=10749%2E400544%2E0pKJR5)
---
Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — **_[but first, can I ask you to take 30 seconds to personally endorse my campaign for Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202607_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk972-su-nd&refcode=jtk972-su-nd&t=2&akid=10749%2E400544%2E0pKJR5)_**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202607_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk972-su-nd&refcode=jtk972-su-nd&t=3&akid=10749%2E400544%2E0pKJR5)
---
This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. **As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will:**
**Build Education That Works for New Mexico by:**
* Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind

* Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day

* Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom

* Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning

* Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes

**Support New Mexico Families by:**
* Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees

* Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet

* Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets

* Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent

* Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back

* Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor

**Back Small Businesses by:**
* Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources

* Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures

* Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty

**Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by:**
* Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico

* Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports

* Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace

* Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits

* Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide

**Strengthen Public Safety by:**
* Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively

* Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare and housing stability

* Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work

* Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need

* Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability

New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you.
**I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them._[Will you please take a quick moment to sign on now?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202607_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk972-su-nd&refcode=jtk972-su-nd&t=4&akid=10749%2E400544%2E0pKJR5)_**

Thank you for your support,

Deb

body:
We join countless Tennesseans, and beyond, in mourning the loss and celebrating the legacy of our friend, Vonda McDaniel, a fearless labor leader, tireless advocate for working people, and cherished member of our Tennessee Democrats family. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134583788/631576395/-1614139448?Refcode=260628-email-dcs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMjg2ZmFkZC0xYjc3LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uWhjXjduRTIW_dfOsf4Ks2CkJZKL0VCA3w0GJFVS9L8=)
---
Peter, We join countless Tennesseans, and beyond, in mourning the loss and celebrating the legacy of our friend, Vonda McDaniel, a fearless labor leader, tireless advocate for working people, and cherished member of our Tennessee Democrats family. For decades, Vonda dedicated her life to fighting for workers across our state. As President of the Central Labor Council of Nashville and Middle Tennessee and Vice President of the AFL-CIO Executive Council from 2017 until June 2026, she helped strengthen Tennessee's labor movement while inspiring generations of organizers and leaders to carry that work forward. A graduate of Tennessee State University, lifetime member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated, active member of First Baptist Church Capitol Hill, and member of Tennessee's delegation to the 2024 Democratic National Convention, Vonda's impact reached every corner of our communities. She had planned to retire from the Central Labor Council at the end of this year to begin a new chapter as Co-Executive Director of the Highlander Center. As Tennessee Democratic Party Chair Rachel Campbell put it: “Vonda was a leader, an advocate, but **most of all our friend**. She showed us how to be fierce while not losing empathy, determined in the face of adversity, and humble in the face of victory. Her work inspired a vision of a better future for a generation of leaders and organizers, and that mentorship will be deeply missed. We send our deepest condolences to her family and loved ones. Ms. Vonda showed us the way, and we honor her by doubling down to deliver for working people.” As we remember Vonda, we also recommit ourselves to the values she lived every day: standing with working families, organizing our communities, and building a Tennessee where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. Our hearts are with her family, friends, union siblings, and everyone whose life she touched. May we honor her memory by continuing the work she dedicated her life to. In solidarity, Tennessee Democratic Party

Peter - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill.

Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did.

I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13.

After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake.

The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today.

And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it.

I won't stand for it. _Not for a second._

clean_body: I was the first in my family to go to college. | Peter - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington. I grew up in the back of a bar. Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did. I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13. I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb. That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way. After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves. That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake. The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today. And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it. I won't stand for it. Not for a second. We are in a fight for the future of this country, and it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. - I didn't come from money. I came from a bar in South Carolina, a mother who worked hard, and a faith that hard work still means something in America. It still does. Thank you for standing with me. God bless you, and God bless South Carolina. | Friends and Supporters,
_I am proud to be an American._

**That’s a sentiment I wake up with every day, but at the moment I feel it more than I ever have in my life**. That’s because our great nation is turning 250 years old this weekend, celebrating the signing of the Declaration of Independence when we broke off the chains of foreign monarchy.

As _President Donald Trump_ —who’s described me as _“an incredible fighter for election integrity”_ who _“will advocate for America First policies”_ —rallies the attention of the country towards the national celebration in Washington DC, remember that the most important moments are happening in your own backyard.

That includes family cookouts where you eat, pray, and party with family and friends, and in local elections which more than any other will decide how well you’ll be able to live in LD27.

_I’m running to return to the Arizona Senate because I believe in protecting America’s laws, her borders, and our elections, and early voting has already started_.

If you’ve already received your early voting form, **cast your ballot for Anthony Kern to be your next state senator** and deploy it to the nearest U.S. Postal Service mailbox.

**You also have the opportunity to vote early in-person at ASU West located at 4701 W THUNDERBIRD RD, GLENDALE, AZ 85306**.

You can still mail back your ballot or vote early in person before the Fourth of July so that when America turns 250-years old, you’ll be secure in the knowledge that you’ve done your country proud, completed your civic duty, and will be represented by conservative champions like myself.

_Turn in your early mail-in ballots and support Anthony Kern for LD27_!

I want to tell you something that’s not easy to talk about...
A sitting Republican elected official recently tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media and wrote:
"I would like to report a foreign occupier. Name: Unpronounceable. Country of origin: Tatooine." He was talking about me. The same official called for the mass deportation of Indian Americans.
I was born in New Delhi. I came to this country as a baby. I grew up in Peoria, Illinois. I went to public schools, got on food stamps for a time with my family, worked my way to Princeton and Harvard Law. I served in government. I got elected to Congress five times.
And someone still looked at all of that and saw a foreign occupier.
I'm telling you this not for sympathy. I'm telling you this because what happened to me is happening to communities all across this country right now, at a scale we have never seen before.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear: if you weren't born here, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
My father came here with nothing. He believed this country would be there for families like ours. It was. Because people fought for it.
That is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help Equal Opportunity Now back the leaders who won't back down? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]

It’s on us to stop the rising tide of MAGA Extremism. And with your help?
We’ll be unstoppable.

If you’d like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-gP0Xd1LL-Lub7Gk22PHy94BMEtGC6mHTmQqNdHOJWNbdJJrdzqEfpr1Cg3-BFcDAgssMiynuTPcIBRxFzq5HdoHDxZp8sIkRxw0WaBo_5kdZZ05iaH_ASIoBWDjdSGFEunbsvnkz9vDqtw8USGMDX2_t-BzfoUwQ7Yi61_HJHrc1Lxe0I7EQpbWbqgxzDYAav8H4K_zRtDbvmfih5-MI1rWu8F3Voy4MrzTedl0-u-iq7Fe2GP3VBQ5ACaM9_scdNSjp7Y5iwF9HrFD2-qDSK5zLQMndSgfmdSl8diU0MtQOkDTq3fLN5Mzqs9wyaRjehzp7yULHQm5AlIXyaUGgg7Yr0NZ4t42imENgy51CQix-Xcq-1-XmRUreAjv0w7M2onPDSFCDAUMSIjUlCLkD7/4s0/Pa3-6o4hQ0OKSr9VcaQmIg/h0/h001.9dJ4Ke9QTtIIlr1y-9B-QpryEkRfTHmkV1EYnRPCPDM)
